note: Password Eye adds a show/hide eye icon to password fields. Its entire behaviour is driven by one config value: password_eye.settings -> password_eye.form_id_password, a comma-separated list of form ids (default user_login_form). hook_form_alter() adds class pwd-see and attaches library password_eye/pwd_eye_lib only to forms whose id is listed; JS toggles the input type between password and text. Settings form at route password_eye.route (/admin/config/system/pssword_eye-settings). No permission of its own, no config schema. Cases are grounded in that real config value: introspection reads back which form ids are targeted; execution edits the list to add a form / restrict to a different form, verified against live config.

evals.prompt: After enabling the password_eye module on a Drupal 11 site, which form gets the show-password eye icon by default, and does it require any configuration to work out of the box?
evals.expected_output: By default it targets the user login form (form id user_login_form, set at install), so the eye icon appears on the login form with no extra configuration.

evals.prompt: How do I make password_eye show its eye icon on additional forms (not just the login form)? Which config value do I change and in what format?
evals.expected_output: Edit password_eye.settings -> password_eye.form_id_password, a comma-separated list of form ids (e.g. user_login_form,user_register_form), via the settings form at /admin/config/system/pssword_eye-settings or drush cset. Any form whose id is listed gets the class pwd-see and the pwd_eye_lib library.

evals.prompt: Technically, how does password_eye make a password field's value visible when the eye is clicked, and which library/CSS classes are involved?
evals.expected_output: hook_form_alter adds class pwd-see and attaches password_eye/pwd_eye_lib; the JS (Drupal.behaviors.pwd) inserts a span.shwpd after each :password input and toggles the input's type between 'password' and 'text' (swapping eye-open/eye-close classes).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, password_eye has been configured to show its eye icon on an extra custom form. Inspect the live configuration and name the custom form id that was added (besides the default login form).
evals.expected_output: The custom form id is pe_custom_form (password_eye.settings:password_eye.form_id_password = 'user_login_form,pe_custom_form').

evals.prompt: Inspect this site's password_eye configuration and state exactly which form id(s) currently receive the eye icon.
evals.expected_output: Only pe_solo_form receives the eye icon (password_eye.settings:password_eye.form_id_password = 'pe_solo_form'); the login form is not included.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, configure password_eye so the show-password eye icon also appears on the user registration form (form id user_register_form), while keeping it on the login form. Apply the change to the live site.
Configure password_eye on this site so the eye icon appears ONLY on the comment form (form id comment_comment_form) and NOT on the login form. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: password_eye.settings:password_eye.form_id_password is set to 'comment_comment_form' (contains comment_comment_form and no longer contains user_login_form).
